topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: Static analysis examines code without requiring every path to execute. Compiler warnings, dedicated analyzers, and guideline checks catch different classes of risk, but each needs the correct compilation context. Harbor’s checked indexing example shows how an explicit interface can eliminate ambiguity before a tool is asked to detect it.

topics.title: 11.1.1 Enabling Strong Warning Levels
topics.summary: Enable a deliberate warning baseline for authored code and review new warnings promptly. Useful diagnostics can expose narrowing conversions, uninitialized values, suspicious conditions, and mismatched declarations. Warning sets differ by compiler and version, so a portable project should express its policy per toolchain rather than copying one universal flag string.

blocks.text: Warnings are not proof of invalid behavior, and silence is not proof of correctness. Investigate the underlying claim. Where a conversion is intentional, make the range argument visible before casting. A cast added only to silence a warning can hide the same defect from both the compiler and the next reviewer.

topics.summary: A large backlog makes meaningful new warnings easy to miss. Reduce it through focused fixes and a ratchet that prevents new debt. Avoid globally disabling a useful warning because one external header or platform adapter needs a narrow exception.

blocks.text: Treat warnings-as-errors as a build policy with a defined scope. Applying it indiscriminately to every transitive third-party source can make a compiler update break a consumer for reasons outside that consumer’s control. Separate authored targets, vendored code, and generated code while retaining visibility into their risks.

blocks.text: Strong warning levels make suspicious constructs visible during compilation, while `-Werror` can prevent known warning debt from silently entering a maintained target.

topics.summary: The signed index is checked before conversion to size_t. That prevents a negative value from becoming a large unsigned index and makes the cast’s justification visible. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run an installed clang-tidy against this chapter and a real compilation database."""
import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("build_directory", type=Path)
args = parser.parse_args()
if not shutil.which("clang-tidy"):
    print("SKIP: clang-tidy is not installed")
    raise SystemExit(77)
if not (args.build_directory / "compile_commands.json").is_file():
    raise SystemExit("configure a supported generator with CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON")
source = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "main.cpp"
raise SystemExit(subprocess.run(["clang-tidy", str(source), "-p", str(args.build_directory)]).returncode)
